Producer evidence for whoever rules on precedence, with file/line citations so a
future flip can run the same producer-safety check `plugin-map`'s flip ran
(objectui#5018 / PR #5156 pinned "neither flattener emits a `map` key").

**The flat spelling is not merely tolerated on gantt — it is what this repo's own
view layers PRODUCE, and neither of them emits a `gantt` key at all.**

`packages/plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx:1209-1218`

```ts
case 'gantt':
  return {
    type: 'object-gantt',
    ...baseProps,
    startDateField: viewOptions.gantt?.startDateField || 'start_date',
    endDateField: viewOptions.gantt?.endDateField || 'end_date',
    progressField: viewOptions.gantt?.progressField || 'progress',
    dependenciesField: viewOptions.gantt?.dependenciesField || 'dependencies',
    ...(viewOptions.gantt || {}),      // SPREAD onto the top level
  };
```

`packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx:2220-2235`

```ts
case 'gantt':
  return {
    type: 'object-gantt',
    ...baseProps,
    ...(schema.data ? { data: schema.data } : {}),
    startDateField: schema.gantt?.startDateField || schema.options?.gantt?.startDateField || 'start_date',
    // …endDateField / progressField / dependenciesField the same way…
    ...(schema.options?.gantt || {}),  // SPREAD onto the top level
    ...(schema.gantt || {}),           // SPREAD onto the top level
  };
```

Both read an authored `gantt` block and **flatten it onto top-level keys**; the
resulting node carries no `gantt` key. So:

* a precedence flip (block wins) would not change what either flattener produces —
  producer-safe by the same check `plugin-map`'s flip used;
* it also means the flat branch is the hot path in practice: every gantt reached
  through `ObjectView` or `ListView` takes it, and a hand-authored `gantt` block
  on such a node would be flattened before `getGanttConfig` ever sees it;
* and it is why objectui#6051 declared the flattened spelling rather than treating
  it as legacy — the repo's own producers emit it.

Cross-reference: objectui#6475 carries the separate question of DECLARING the
`gantt` block (severed from PR #6472). That card and this one are independent —
declaring the block face changes no precedence, and flipping precedence needs no
declaration.

**Dispatched** by the `domain:ui` seat.

**Read the triage comment on this card before the body.** The body says "which face wins is a ruling, not a dev call" — that was true when it was filed, and it has since been ruled. Triage graded it via sibling-ruling inheritance and set the charter, quoted here verbatim:

> Charter: flip precedence to block-wins + dev-mode warning naming the losing face's keys, mirroring PR #5156's mechanics. Fork clause: if implementation surfaces a gantt-specific semantic difference from the map case, STOP and report — inheritance covers the shape, not a measured divergence.

The maintainer ruling being inherited, also verbatim:

> Precedence flip (maintainer ruling on objectui#5018, 2026-08-17): the `map` block wins over the internal flat spelling, with a dev-mode warning naming the ignored top-level keys.

So both halves are settled: **the `gantt` block wins, and the losing face's keys get named in a dev-mode warning instead of being dropped silently.** Do not re-open either. The fork clause is your only exit, and it is a stop-and-report, not a licence to choose.

**Re-measure on today's main — the code the card quotes has moved under it.** PR #6472 merged after this card was filed. It retyped `getGanttConfig`'s parameter, moved nine members from the plugin-private `GanttConfigEx` into `GanttConfig`, and declared 27 keys on `ObjectGanttSchema`. The two-branch shape and the early `return` should still be there, but read the function as it stands rather than trusting the excerpt above it.

**Producer safety is the check that makes this flip safe, and it must be re-run, not inherited.** The card's second comment measured that `ObjectView` and `ListView` both flatten their gantt options onto top-level keys and emit no `gantt` key at all, so a flip strands neither. That is the same check `plugin-map`'s flip pinned, and it was measured before #6472 landed. Re-run it on today's main and show the result. Then run the zero-casualty scan for nodes carrying **both** spellings, since those are the only ones whose rendering actually changes — and state the limit of that scan out loud the way #6472 did for #6475: an in-repo census measures this tree, and authored metadata outside it is exactly what it cannot see.

**Note what the producer evidence implies for your warning.** Because both view layers flatten, the flat branch is the hot path in practice — a hand-authored `gantt` block reaching `ObjectGantt` through `ObjectView` or `ListView` has already been flattened before `getGanttConfig` sees it. Make sure your dev-mode warning fires on the case that actually reaches it and does not spray on every flattened node.

⛔ **Do not declare the `gantt` block face.** That is #6475, severed from #6472 by PM ruling because it changes a published CLI's refusal behaviour, and it is waiting on a human. The two are independent: declaring the block face changes no precedence, and flipping precedence needs no declaration. Your PR must not make `gantt` a declared key.

**Reverse verification.** Predict RED and observe it: a node carrying both spellings must render the block's values after your change and must have rendered the flat ones before. Pin the warning too — assert it names the ignored keys, and prove that assertion can fail. Prove any file mutation on disk rather than by an editor's exit code, and restore by hash.

**Fence and hygiene.**
- Dedicated per-task worktree before your first edit. A feature branch on the shared checkout is not enough — its HEAD gets switched under you.
- ⛔ Never `git stash`. The stack lives in the common git directory and is shared by every worktree; a `pop` can restore another agent's work and reports success.
- ⛔ Do not touch `content/docs/releases/`. Your release-notes input is the changeset.
- Claim first: assign yourself, post a claim comment with your session ID and branch, and re-read this thread before writing code.
- **Run tests narrowly** — the shared validation lock is a cross-agent resource and a wide run has been measured holding it nearly eighteen minutes.

**#6470 and #6471 sit on this same hot file and are queued behind you.** Report your exact file face so they can be released. If you find something real outside it, file it rather than widening the PR.
